title: Juicy Garlicky Argentinian Beef Empanadas
description: A traditional Argentinian dish featuring garlicky beef and a crispy pastry crust, perfect for a meal prep lunch or dinner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large skillet, heat the ghee over medium high heat.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Stir in the chopped nuka pickle and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Season the beef mixture with salt and black pepper to taste.
Roll out the empanada pastry dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of the beef mixture onto the center of each dough circle.
Brush the edges of the dough with the beaten egg for a golden glaze.
Fold the dough in half over the filling and press the edges together to seal.
Brush the tops of the empanadas with the remaining egg wash and bake for 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
